title: How Organizations Actually Use AI: 17 Million Enterprise Messages
hook: Linking ChatGPT Enterprise records to company financials shows who really adopts AI at work: large, R&D-heavy firms — with early-career staff driving the heaviest use.
key_points: Links ChatGPT Enterprise account records to usage, worker roles, task classifications, and public-company financials through March 2026.
The six-month-adoption worker sample alone covers 1,500+ organizations and 17M+ messages, analyzed privacy-preservingly.
Usage grew from both new firms adopting and existing adopters using it more intensively.
Among U.S. public companies, adoption concentrates in larger, more valuable, more R&D- and SG&A-intensive firms.
Active use spans job functions and seniority, with the highest intensity among early-career workers.
Tasks span knowledge work broadly: writing, technical work, communication, and information synthesis.
content_html: Most claims about "AI at work" rest on surveys or anecdotes. Aaron Chatterji and co-authors (arXiv, August 2026) instead link ChatGPT Enterprise account records to usage logs, worker roles, task classifications, and public-company financial data through March 2026 — a privacy-preserving view of adoption at scale. The six-month-adoption worker sample alone spans more than 1,500 organizations and over 17 million messages.
extra_html:
Four facts

Usage grew rapidly, from a mix of new firms signing on and existing adopters ramping up intensity. Among U.S.-based public companies, adoption skews toward larger, more valuable firms with higher R&D and SG&A intensity. Within adopting firms, active use spans job functions and seniority levels — with the highest intensity among early-career workers. And the task mix is broad knowledge work: writing, technical work, communication, and information synthesis.

Why it matters

The headline is dispersion. Firms differ widely in the speed, breadth, and purpose of enterprise AI adoption, which the authors read as evidence that organizations are still actively figuring out how to fit these tools into their workflows. Note the vantage point: this is one vendor's enterprise product, so it describes ChatGPT Enterprise customers rather than the whole market.
